title: REDI-NET L-2 Leech Processing
author: REDI-NET Consortium
materials: If leeches are about a pinky fingernail size, homogenize leech tissues as section 3. Add 400 µL 1x PBS and 100 µL ATL-DX buffer in a Thermo Scientific Screw Cap 1.5 mL Micro tube containing 0.1 mm beads from the step 3 in "Before Start" section.
Select the program IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Flex_4wash on the instrument.
Select program IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Duo_4wash on the instrument.

If leeches are about a pinky fingernail size, homogenize leech tissues as section 3. Add 400 µL 1x PBS and 100 µL ATL-DX buffer in a Thermo Scientific Screw Cap 1.5 mL Micro tube containing 0.1 mm beads from the step 3 in "Before Start" section.

steps.title: Sample Preparation and Morphological Examination
steps.instruction: Identify and prepare leech samples for processing.

substeps.instruction: Morphologically examine leeches from each vial (fresh or stored at -80 °C) to identify species; keep only parasitic Euhirudinea and discard others.
Clean forceps with 70% ethanol and Kimwipes before use and between samples.

steps.title: Leech Washing and Initial Processing
steps.instruction: Clean the leech and prepare it for tissue/blood meal extraction.

substeps.instruction: Rinse leech with 70% ethanol.
Place the rinsed leech on Kimwipes to absorb ethanol residuals, then place in a petri dish on ice.
Wash the leech three times sequentially in petri dishes on ice using ice-cold 1x PBS to remove external contaminants.

steps.title: Blood Meal and Organ Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract the blood meal and internal organ samples from the leech.

substeps.instruction: Cut across the middle of the leech using scissors.
Drip as much of the blood meal as possible into a petri dish.
Transfer the blood meal to a 1.5 mL tube by pipetting.
Place the leech back into the petri dish and use a scalpel to cut it open longitudinally.
Open the leech with forceps and use a sterile cotton swab to thoroughly wipe the opened inner organs.
Place the cotton tip of the swab into a 1.5 mL tube and cut off the plastic handle.

steps.title: Leech Tissue Processing
steps.instruction: Prepare leech tissue samples for lysis.

substeps.instruction: Label navy RINO RNA lysis tubes on the cap (avoid labeling sides).
Add 60 µL cold, sterile 1x PBS into each navy RINO tube.
Using an empty Petri dish on ice, cut the leech from head to tail and trim tissue into small pieces approximately 3 mm x 3 mm.
Add one piece of 3 mm x 3 mm leech tissue into a navy RINO tube.

steps.title: Sample Lysis and Homogenization
steps.instruction: Homogenize the blood meal, cotton swabs, and tissue samples using a Bullet Blender.

substeps.instruction: For blood meal processing, add 50 µL blood meal to a prepared tube. For leeches without blood meal, use only the cotton swab.
Add 80 µL ATL-DTX buffer into the tube.
Load tubes (blood meal, cotton tip, or leech tissue lysate) into the fully cooled Bullet Blender; refill dry ice compartment if necessary.
Set speed to 10 and time to 00:03:00 and press Start.
Remove tubes and visually inspect. If homogenization is incomplete, repeat at speed 10 for 00:03:00.
Centrifuge the suspension at 100 x g for 1 minute to pellet debris.

steps.title: Secondary Homogenization (Tissue)
steps.instruction: Perform additional beating for tissue samples if required.

substeps.instruction: Load RINO tubes with leech tissue into the Bullet Blender (ensure dry ice is replenished).
Set speed to 12 and time to 00:05:00 and press Start.
Let samples settle for 00:01:00, then repeat the beating process.
Centrifuge the tubes with lysate at 12,000 x g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Control Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare positive and negative controls for each batch.

substeps.instruction: Positive Control: Transfer 37.5 µL ZymoBIOMICS Microbial Community Standard Material, 100 µL EBV, and 100 µL DENV-1 standard into a Screw Cap 1.5 mL MicroTube containing 0.1 mm beating beads. Add 162.5 µL 1x PBS and 100 µL ATL-DX buffer.
Negative Control: Add 400 µL sterile 1x PBS and 100 µL ATL-DX Buffer to a Screw Cap 1.5 mL MicroTube containing 0.1 mm beating beads.

steps.title: Nucleic Acid Extraction (KingFisher Flex - 96 Well)
steps.instruction: Extract TNA using the KingFisher Flex instrument.

substeps.instruction: Confirm 96 deep-well magnetic heads and 96 well deep-well heat blocks are used.
Load program 'IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Flex_4wash' onto the instrument.

Set up plates: Elution (Nuclease-free water, 75 µL), Wash 4 (100% ethanol, 750 µL), Wash 3 (80% ethanol, 750 µL), Wash 2 (Buffer AW2, 700 µL), Wash 1 (Buffer AW1, 700 µL), and Sample (Lysate and lysis buffer, 985 µL). Note: Do not use kit elution buffer.
Add 20 µL Proteinase K to wells of a new deep-well plate.
Carefully transfer the top 320 µL supernatant from the lysed samples (without particle carryover) to the wells containing Proteinase K. This is the Sample Plate.

Prepare a master mix (with 10% overage) of 135 µL Buffer VXL, 540 µL Buffer ACB, and 25 µL MagAttract Suspension G per sample. Mix slowly (or on Hula mixer for 2 min) to avoid foaming. Add 700 µL of this mixture to each sample.
Start the run and load plates when prompted.
After the ~35 minute run, immediately remove the elution plate and cover it or transfer eluate to storage tubes.

steps.title: Nucleic Acid Extraction (KingFisher Duo - Low Throughput)
steps.instruction: Extract TNA using the KingFisher Duo Prime instrument.

substeps.instruction: Confirm 12-tip magnetic head and 12 well deep-well heat blocks are used.
Load program 'IndiMag_Pathogen_KF_Duo_4wash' onto the instrument.
Set up Sample Plate: Row A (Lysate/lysis buffer, 985 µL), Row B (Buffer AW1, 700 µL), Row C (Buffer AW2, 700 µL), Row D (80% ethanol, 750 µL), Row E (100% ethanol, 750 µL), Row F (Tip comb, 700 µL).
Set up Elution Strip: Row A (Nuclease-free water, 75 µL). Note: Do not use kit elution buffer.
Add 20 µL Proteinase K to the sample row.
Transfer 270 µL supernatant (without particle carryover) to the sample row containing Proteinase K.
Prepare a master mix (with 10% overage) of 135 µL Buffer VXL, 540 µL Buffer ACB, and 20 µL MagAttract Suspension G per sample. Mix slowly to avoid foaming. Add 695 µL of this mixture to each sample.
Start the run and load the plate/strip when prompted.
After the ~35 minute run, immediately remove the elution strip and transfer eluate to storage.

steps.title: Quantification and Storage
steps.instruction: Measure nucleic acid concentration and store samples.

substeps.instruction: Use 1 µL of total nucleic acid for DNA and RNA concentration measurement using a Qubit 4 Fluorometer (using Qubit 1X dsDNA HS and RNA HS Assay Kits) following manufacturer instructions.
Store samples at -20 °C for less than 2 weeks, or at -80 °C for long-term storage.
Alternatively, proceed with testing following REDI-NET SOP L-4.
